transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. 

I guess what finally made me make the appointment is... well, my appetite has just been sort of all over the place for the last few months. It's probably not a huge deal, but I've had stretches where I just end up skipping dinner, and I've actually lost a little weight without really trying to. Or, um, other nights I'll just pick at some crackers or a bowl of cereal because cooking for myself just feels a bit... pointless right now? 

I know that sounds a little silly, especially since I'm a social worker in healthcare myself and I should probably be managing my routines better, but... does that make sense? I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by coming in to get it checked out.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much pleasure or interest out of things that you used to enjoy?

I mean, I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest. I still try to keep up with my routines, you know? I still go out and water the garden, and I make sure to show up to my book club so I don't let anyone down. 

It's just... well, lately, I guess I'm mostly just going through the motions. It all feels a bit flat, if that makes sense? I find myself leaving book club early, or sometimes I'll look at the garden and just... not start. I know I should be more engaged, and I'm really trying, I promise. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes?
Can you tell me if you've been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Oh, um, no, I don't think so. I wouldn't really use the word depressed. I mean, I have my moments where I feel a little blue, maybe, but certainly not most of the day or every day. 

I really try to keep a positive outlook, you know? In my line of work, you see people going through so much, so I'd feel awful complaining when I have so much to be grateful for. It's really just that... that sort of flat feeling I mentioned before. But I'm definitely not sitting around crying all the time or anything like that. 

Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not, um, overstating things.
Have you noticed a decrease in your ability to feel pleasure or enjoyment in activities, even when you participate in them?

Um, I think that's pretty similar to what we were just talking about, right? With the garden and the book club? 

Like I said, I'm still doing things, and I wouldn't say I've lost the ability to enjoy them entirely. I still smile when we talk about a good chapter at book club, or when the roses bloom. It's just... maybe the feeling doesn't stick around as long as it used to? Or it takes a little more effort to get there. 

But I'm still participating, and I'm still trying my best to be present. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I know I'm still functioning fine. Does that answer your question, doctor? I hope I'm being helpful.
Can you describe how long these feelings of flatness or reduced pleasure have been going on? Have they been present most days for at least two years?

Oh, um... two years? No, no, I don't think it's been quite that long. I really don't want you to think I've just been letting things slide for years on end without trying to fix it. 

I guess... well, if I really think about it, it started around the time the divorce was finalized. Which was, um, about a year and seven months ago? Give or take? 

I mean, that's a normal reaction, right? To feel a little off after something like that? I've really been doing my best to push through and keep things normal since then. I hope I'm not making it sound like I've just been wallowing this whole time. Is a year and a half something to be worried about?
Have you experienced any days where you felt particularly low, tired, or like you weren't good enough, even when things seemed okay on the surface?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I feel completely inadequate or anything like that. At work, I know I'm doing a good job, and I try to keep my energy up. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, there are times when I get a little stuck in my own head. 

It's mostly just about the divorce. I find myself... well, I keep sort of replaying the marriage in my mind. And I catch myself telling myself that I must have just failed at something really basic. 

Which is silly, I know! I mean, part of me knows perfectly well that relationships are much more complicated than just one person failing. I work in healthcare, I see complex family dynamics every day, so I really should know better than to think that way. 

I try to brush it off quickly, so it's not like it ruins my whole day. It's just a thought that creeps in sometimes when I'm tired. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound too foolish admitting that... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture.
Have you had days where your mood felt consistently low or down, nearly all day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Two weeks straight? Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's been like that. I really try not to let myself get stuck in a rut for that long. 

I mean, sure, I have days where I feel a bit down, especially if I'm tired from work or... or just thinking too much. But I always try to pull myself together. I'll make sure I go to work, put on a smile, and get things done. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself for weeks on end. 

So, no, I don't think I've had a whole two-week stretch where I felt down nearly all day. I always manage to bounce back at least a little bit. That's a good sign, right? I'm trying my best to stay positive.
Have you ever had a period where you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Oh, um... I know you just asked about that, and I really hope I didn't answer it wrong the first time! But... no, I really haven't ever had a period like that. 

Even at my absolute worst, right after the papers were signed, I never let it get to the point where I was down all day, every day for weeks. I have my clients at the clinic relying on me, you know? I couldn't just check out like that. I always make it a point to push through and be there for them. 

So, no, definitely not two whole weeks of feeling depressed most of the day. Is that... is it okay that I don't have that? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
